answer: Latency-triangulation locality proof: at random, attester beacons ping each identity from many geographic vantage points and record round-trip times, and the light-speed delays triangulate a physical position no software can forge. A falcon-eyed auditor collapses any identities whose coordinates and network routes coincide into a single slot. So 1000 sybils on one datacenter box resolve to one identity; to look spread out an operator must rent 1000 machines in distant regions, each burning its own monthly hosting ember, and any co-located pair caught loses its standing.
